rulings.restated: Input — Has the American opportunity credit been claimed (by you or anyone else) for this student for any 4 tax years before 2025?
rulings.model: The eligible-student gate uses the TIN helper that allows a student who has only 'applied for' an ITIN/ATIN; the IRS AOC text requires the student to have been 'issued a TIN by the due date'.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: interface gap; p970 p. 11 (not among the reviewer's pages): "If an ATIN or ITIN is applied for on or before the due date of a 2025 return (including extensions) and the IRS issues an ATIN or ITIN as a result of the application, the IRS will consider the ATIN or ITIN as issued on or before the due date of the return." i8863 p. 3, item 5: "Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." The model read the i8863 sentence correctly, but the pages it got omit the Pub. 970 rule that treats an ITIN or ATIN applied for by the due date, and then issued, as issued by the due date; under it the English of dependent.tin ("issued on or before the due date ... or have you applied for an ITIN or ATIN for this person by then") and household.all_tin ("or have applied for an ITIN") say what the source allows, as ruled in Stage 19 round 1 (person.findings.md, Checked, not findings). Line 23's own question matches, as the model says; the TIN test sits in the eligible-student gate. Why this line is new this round: the render prompt changed from round 2 only in dependent.qr_relationship (lawful now also for sibling_descendant), the dependent.lawful question and the dependent.edu_over label (diff of .transcription/dependent.render.prompt.txt against the round-2 archive); the text the model objects to is unchanged and was judged MATCH last round, so the new MISMATCH is reviewer variance, not the lawful change or its English.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: interface gap; p970 p. 11 (not among the reviewer's pages): "If an ATIN or ITIN is applied for on or before the due date of a 2025 return (including extensions) and the IRS issues an ATIN or ITIN as a result of the application, the IRS will consider the ATIN or ITIN as issued on or before the due date of the return." i8863 p. 3, item 5: "Filers and students must have been issued a TIN by the due date of their 2025 return (including extensions)." The model read the i8863 sentence correctly, but the pages it got omit the Pub. 970 rule that treats an ITIN or ATIN applied for by the due date, and then issued, as issued by the due date; under it the English of dependent.tin ("issued on or before the due date ... or have you applied for an ITIN or ATIN for this person by then") and household.all_tin ("or have applied for an ITIN") say what the source allows, as ruled in Stage 19 round 1 (person.findings.md, Checked, not findings). The line's arithmetic is not disputed; the model objects only to the American opportunity gate (dependent.edu_aoc, household.all_tin for the filers). Why this line is new this round: the render prompt changed from round 2 only in dependent.qr_relationship (lawful now also for sibling_descendant), the dependent.lawful question and the dependent.edu_over label (diff of .transcription/dependent.render.prompt.txt against the round-2 archive); the text the model objects to is unchanged and was judged MATCH last round, so the new MISMATCH is reviewer variance, not the lawful change or its English.
